title: Day 693 — Sheinbaum Announces Push to Bar Dual Nationals From Presidency, Governorships
detail: On August 25, 2026 (Day 693, Tuesday), President Sheinbaum said her government is preparing a constitutional reform initiative to prohibit dual nationals from serving as president or state governor, asking rhetorically "¿por qué vas a tener doble nacionalidad si representas al pueblo de México?" The proposal was triggered by the case of former Tamaulipas governor Francisco Javier García Cabeza de Vaca, who holds Mexican and U.S. nationality and has lived in the United States since 2022 despite an active Mexican arrest warrant for organized crime and money laundering; Mexico's extradition request has gone unanswered. Sheinbaum called him "un prófugo de la ley." Cabeza de Vaca responded that the Mexican Constitution currently permits him to run for president. The next step is formal filing of the initiative in Congress, where the scope of the restriction — president only, or governors too — will be debated.

media.caption: Sheinbaum announces a planned constitutional reform to bar dual nationals from the presidency and governorships

title: Day 693 — US Consulate Issues Security Alert for Mexicali Over Possible Cartel Attack Plot
detail: On August 25, 2026 (Day 693, Tuesday), the U.S. Consulate in Tijuana issued a security alert for Mexicali, Baja California, suspending official U.S. personnel travel and activities in the city and advising citizens to avoid government buildings after intelligence pointed to a possible attack threat. Reporting attributed the alert to intercepted communications suggesting "Los Rusos" — the armed wing of the Sinaloa Cartel's Mayo Zambada faction, led by Juan José Ponce Félix ("El Ruso," $5M US bounty) — was planning attacks on Municipal Police installations and the State Attorney General's Office. President Sheinbaum confirmed the alert originated from U.S. agencies but said Mexico's security cabinet had "no información que confirme una amenaza directa," adding: "No hay más información de qué pudiera ser esta alerta, sino sencillamente de estar atentos y con vigilancia en Mexicali." Baja California Governor Marina del Pilar Ávila and federal forces reinforced presence in the city; recent operations against the group had seized 120 kg of fentanyl pills (~4 million doses) and arrested at least 15 members over the prior two months.

media.caption: Sheinbaum addresses the US security alert for Mexicali at her morning press conference

title: Day 693 — Sinaloa Congress Names Graciela Domínguez Nava Interim Governor, 31-6
detail: On August 25, 2026 (Day 693, Tuesday), the Sinaloa Congress voted 31 in favor to 6 against, with zero abstentions, to designate Graciela Domínguez Nava as interim governor, resolving the succession question left open when the legislature approved Rubén Rocha Moya's indefinite leave on August 23. The session had originally been scheduled for Monday, August 24 but was suspended and reconvened the following day. Domínguez Nava, a Morena sociologist and former Sinaloa state deputy (2018–2021) and Secretary of Public Education and Culture (2021–2024) who was also serving as federal deputy for Mazatlán's District 1 before taking leave in June, becomes the state's third governor of 2026 after Rocha Moya and interim predecessor Yeraldine Bonilla Valverde.

media.caption: Graciela Domínguez Nava is sworn in as interim governor of Sinaloa
